title: 2017 AMC 10B Problem 12
statement: Elmer’s new car gets \(50\%\) better fuel efficiency, measured in kilometers per liter, than his old car. However, his new car uses diesel fuel, which is \(20\%\) more expensive per liter than the gasoline his old car uses. By what percent will Elmer save money if he uses his new car instead of his old car for a long trip?

solutions.text:
Let the old car’s fuel efficiency be \(M\) kilometers per liter and let gasoline cost \(C\) dollars per liter. The old car therefore costs \(\dfrac CM\) dollars per kilometer to fuel.

The new car gets \(1.5M\) kilometers per liter and its fuel costs \(1.2C\) dollars per liter, so its fuel cost per kilometer is \[\dfrac{1.2C}{1.5M}=0.8\dfrac CM.\]

The new fuel cost is \(80\%\) of the old one, so Elmer saves \(20\%.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: Compare cost per kilometer, not cost per liter
New fuel uses fewer liters but each liter costs more
